label: TMUA Specimen · Paper 2 · Question 10

hints.title: Read which quantity is the base
hints.body: Use the definition y=logx2⟺xy=2 and retain the restriction x>1.
hints.recap: A logarithm is an exponent; here its base varies.
hints.pitfall: Do not treat this as the usual graph with base 2 and input x.
hints.pause: Consider which signs of y can make the power equal to 2.

recall.reminder: Translate a logarithm to a power before comparing possible graphs.

hints.title: Calculate a few exact landmarks
hints.body: In the power equation, choose y=1,2,12 and solve for the corresponding x-values. Then consider what happens when the base gets close to 1 from above.
hints.recap: Exact points and end behaviour can distinguish sketches.
hints.pitfall: The domain boundary is excluded, so do not assign it a finite plotted value without checking.
hints.pause: Calculate the points and use them, together with your sign test, to select a sketch.

recall.reminder: Use integer and fractional index laws to produce exact graph checks.

solution:
Rewrite the relation as xy=2. Since x>1, y must be positive: nonpositive exponents would give a value at most 1.

The graph passes through (2, 2), (2, 1) and (4, 12). Increasing the base reduces the positive exponent needed to obtain 2, so the function decreases.

As x approaches 1 from above, y grows without bound; as x grows without bound, y approaches 0 from above. Only graph E has these properties.
